bits.text: I stand on a stage in a robe. I say a man walks into a noodle shop, four noble truths, the table goes quiet. Twenty-five centuries and my best crowd work is the fourteen questions I refuse to answer. Not the answers, just the napkins.

bits.text: Enlightenment has a merch table. I'm not proud of that. The robe started as renunciation — give up everything, own nothing, walk the road. Twenty-five centuries later it's got a logo. Four logos, actually. Theravada, Mahayana, Zen, and Tibet, which went with rainbows, because nothing says "I have transcended material desire" like a color palette.
